name: CameraAccessSpec
source_title: CameraAccess.crysl — requested canonical CrySL source (not found)
protocol: Unverified, non-CrySL reconstruction: open_camera → (onOpened | CameraAccessException(CAMERA_DISCONNECTED)); close_camera → onClosed. No authoritative CameraAccess.crysl ORDER expression was found.
important_note: The canonical CrySL raw URL was attempted and reportedly returned HTTP 404. Therefore no CameraAccessSpec rule text, governed-class declaration, events, predicates, or formal lifecycle can be attributed to a primary CrySL source. The required applies_to_types entry is a naming-convention-required unresolved detector target: Android documentation identifies android.hardware.camera2.CameraAccessException, not a public android.hardware.camera2.CameraAccess type. It must not be treated as evidence that this Android API type exists or that the finding proves a security defect.

events.name: open_camera
events.condition: Observed when source contains an invocation matching an Android Camera2 camera-opening call. Observation alone does not satisfy a successful-open predicate: opening is asynchronous, and success requires evidence of the applicable StateCallback.onOpened callback.

events.name: camera_opened
events.condition: Observed when a CameraDevice.StateCallback.onOpened implementation or invocation is present. A successful-open predicate is satisfied only when the callback is associated with the applicable open request and reached at runtime; source presence alone does not prove callback delivery.

events.name: camera_disconnected
events.condition: Observed when code catches, creates, tests, or reports CameraAccessException/CAMERA_DISCONNECTED. A disconnection-reason predicate is satisfied only by evidence that the exception reason equals CameraAccessException.CAMERA_DISCONNECTED; an openCamera call, catch clause, diagnostic message, or mere reference to the constant does not establish that reason.

events.name: close_camera
events.condition: Observed when close is invoked on a camera-device reference or an onClosed callback is implemented/invoked. Teardown completion is satisfied only with the applicable StateCallback.onClosed callback; invoking close() alone does not establish immediate reusability.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that a public Android API type named android.hardware.camera2.CameraAccess exists.
Do not infer that CameraAccessSpec is a canonical CROSSINGTUD CrySL rule; the requested CameraAccess.crysl primary URL was unavailable.
Do not infer that an observed openCamera call successfully opened a camera.
Do not infer CAMERA_DISCONNECTED merely from a CameraAccessException catch or from the detector message.

Do not infer that another app is using the camera from CAMERA_DISCONNECTED. Android also documents removable-camera removal, an invalidated camera ID, and service shutdown due to a higher-priority request as possible causes.
Do not infer that calling close() has completed teardown or that a subsequent open will succeed.
Do not infer a security vulnerability, permission failure, exclusive-access violation, or resource leak from this finding alone.
semantic_scope: The representative finding concerns a local camera-open operation in net.sourceforge.opencamera.preview.PreviewSurface.openCamera and a diagnostic referring to Android Camera2 CameraAccessException.CAMERA_DISCONNECTED. In the absence of a verified CameraAccess.crysl rule, the detector can at most be described as observing source-level camera-opening and exception-related patterns; it does not establish a broader typestate, access-ownership, or security property.

detector_semantics.claim: At the reported method, the detector associates a camera-access/opening path with a CAMERA_DISCONNECTED diagnostic.
predicates: An Android Camera2 opening call is present or resolved at the reported location.
A CameraAccessException/CAMERA_DISCONNECTED diagnostic or matching exception-handling pattern is present.
For a true disconnected-reason predicate, the exception reason must be evidenced as CameraAccessException.CAMERA_DISCONNECTED.
limitations: No primary CameraAccess.crysl source was found, so these predicates are not a recovered CrySL rule.
Static source matching cannot prove that a runtime exception occurred, its reason, camera ownership, callback ordering, device availability, or recovery outcome.
The supplied prose message is not equivalent to Android's complete documented causes for CAMERA_DISCONNECTED.
The reported class and method do not, without the exact source revision and resolved call graph, prove that CameraManager.openCamera is reached directly rather than via an abstraction or not at all.

documented_behavior: Android Camera2 uses CameraManager to enumerate, query, and open camera devices.
CameraAccessException is used when a device cannot be queried or opened, or when an opened CameraDevice connection is no longer valid.
CAMERA_DISCONNECTED can mean a removable camera was disconnected, the camera ID is no longer valid, or the camera service closed the connection because of a higher-priority access request.
CameraManager.openCamera requires CAMERA permission and can throw CameraAccessException when the camera is disabled, disconnected, or used by a higher-priority client.
preconditions: For CameraManager.openCamera, the caller needs Manifest.permission.CAMERA.
The camera ID, callback, and executor or handler argument appropriate to the overload must be non-null and valid.
A successful asynchronous open must be evidenced through the relevant CameraDevice.StateCallback rather than presumed from invocation alone.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: At runtime, CAMERA_DISCONNECTED denotes an Android Camera2 access failure with multiple documented environmental or service-level causes; it does not by itself identify another application as the cause.

A catch of CameraAccessException that handles CAMERA_DISABLED, CAMERA_IN_USE, MAX_CAMERAS_IN_USE, CAMERA_ERROR, or an unspecified reason rather than CAMERA_DISCONNECTED.

A source-level openCamera call for which asynchronous onOpened later succeeds.
A disconnect caused by removable hardware removal, camera-ID invalidation, or priority arbitration but reported as though another app exclusively owns the camera.
A close() call reported as lifecycle completion even though onClosed has not yet occurred.
